note: Distilled from the reference research of 11 November 2026 (ScrollTide, Navbar Gallery, Refero, Footer Design, 21st.dev, Watermelon UI, Motion.dev, Spline, Paper Shaders, Manus). Patterns are described in our own words. Script sizes are approximate; Spline was not measured.

techniques.name: CSS scroll-driven animations
techniques.use: Scroll-linked reveals, progress bars and parallax with no script, where the browser supports animation-timeline.
techniques.fallback: Elements show in their final state where it is not supported.
techniques.reducedMotion: Wrapped in a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference query.

techniques.name: View Transitions
techniques.use: Shared-element and crossfade changes between pages and states.

techniques.name: SVG drawing and animated SVG
techniques.use: Lines that draw themselves, drifting paths, authored illustrations that move.

techniques.name: Motion (vanilla, motion.dev)
techniques.use: UI animation: in-view staggers, springs, scroll-linked transforms and timed sequences, without React.
techniques.needs: the motion package (animate, scroll, inView, stagger); motion/mini is about 3 KB for animate only
techniques.reducedMotion: Check prefers-reduced-motion and skip the animation.

techniques.name: GSAP with ScrollTrigger
techniques.use: Pinned scroll stories and scrubbed timelines across several elements.
techniques.needs: gsap and ScrollTrigger (own licence: confirm it allows the client site)
techniques.fallback: The sections in normal flow with no pinning.
techniques.reducedMotion: No pinning or scrubbing; the content shows in order.

techniques.name: Own GLSL shader
techniques.use: A noise, liquid, distortion or grain background drawn by the graphics card, behind a few sections.
techniques.needs: Plain WebGL with the harness's own shader code
techniques.fallback: A CSS gradient in the same colours, painted first.

techniques.name: Paper Shaders
techniques.use: Ready shader effects and image filters: mesh gradient, grain gradient, fluted glass, halftone, liquid metal.
techniques.needs: @paper-design/shaders pinned to an exact version (breaking changes ship in patch versions)
techniques.fallback: A CSS gradient or a pre-rendered image.

techniques.name: Three.js scene
techniques.use: A custom 3D object or scene the visitor can turn or explore, loaded after the page.
techniques.fallback: A poster image or short video.

techniques.name: Spline scene
techniques.use: A designed 3D scene from the operator's own Spline file, with events wired to the page.
techniques.needs: @splinetool/runtime (size not measured; treat it as heavy and opt-in)

techniques.name: React Three Fiber
techniques.use: Declarative Three.js in React. Not in this starter: it needs a React integration, so use three-scene instead.

techniques.name: Framer Motion (React)
techniques.use: React animation. Not in this starter: it needs a React integration, so use motion-dev, the same library without React.
